title: FLORA VETERANS DAY
full_story:
Flora American Legion Post #14 reminds residents about the observance of what was originally called Armistice Day.  It honored the end of World War I in Europe and was always observed when the war officially ended, on the 11th hour, of the 11th day of the 11th month.  Later, it transformed into Veterans Day, a day to honor the service of all who serve or have served in the U.S. Military services.  This year’s observance is today at the Memorial in Library Park.

At 10:15 am all units assemble behind the American Legion on Mill Street.  Legion members will be joined by the Floyd Henson Jr. High School Band, the Flora Boy Scout Troop #8282, and the Shooting Stars Drill Team.  The parade steps off at 10:30 am and marches to the memorial.  Organizers have told WNOI that there will be side-by-sides in the parade to allow any Veteran who would like to ride in the parade route.  Please be there at 10:15.

At Library Park, seating will be available for Veterans and family members who cannot stand for the duration of the ceremony.  The program includes the Marching Pups perform the Star-Spangled Banner.  The Pledge of Allegiance will be said, and Jim Earlywine will introduce the speaker Lee Ryker.  The Honor guard will lower the flag to half staff and fires a 21 Gun Salute and then Taps is played.  The tornado sirens will then sound at 11:00 am.  Following the ceremony attendees are invited to a meal served at VFW Post #3999 across from the Memorial.

title: CLAY COUNTY BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Clay County Board met last night, Circuit Clerk Crystal Ballard asked board members to delay passing the budget so employee pay could be amended.  Ballard read a statement alongside letters of praise from Judge J-C Powless and Assistant Judge Amanda Ade-Harlow advocating for the department’s two deputy clerks.  However, Board Chairman Joe Goodman noted that the board is mandated to pass the budget at its November meeting.  Goodman stated the board will revisit the salary issue in January or February and revise the budget if necessary.

The 2027 budget passed with a nearly five-percent increase to the county tax levy.  In addition, a series of short-term fund transfers were approved to support the Cooperative Extension, Mentally Deficient, and Mental Health funds until tax revenues are collected.

In other business, the board approved a new Clay County Food Ordinance.  The measure authorizes the county to license and regulate all food establishments in both incorporated and unincorporated areas.  It also tasks the Health Department with establishing a sanitation program for mobile food units.

Meanwhile, the Health Department is partnering with the Regional Office of Education and the Dolly Parton Imagination Library to bring youth literacy books to Clay County.  The department is also applying for an After School grant to expand its “Beyond the Bell” programming to children ages six to ten.

Looking ahead, a swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for November 17th following the recent election. Taking the oath of office will be County Clerk Amy Britton, Treasurer Stacey Allen, Sheriff Andy Myers, and seven county board members.  Chairman Goodman also recognized long-time board member Dave Johnson, who is retiring after serving since 2013.

title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board met Tuesday evening, a week later than their regularly scheduled meeting date, which coincided with election day last week.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order and trustees quickly approved the past meeting minutes and the bills.

With no visitors present, the mayor moved straight into the officers report.  Delonshaw noted that at the last meeting they opted to seek bids to install rip rap at the village sewer lagoon, to prevent erosion.  He said since it is getting later into Fall, its unlikely the project will be completed soon.  To further encourage the bidding process, he suggested extending the project completion date to 12 months, to give companies time to complete the work.  After some discussion, trustees unanimously agreed with the mayor’s suggestion and extended the completion date to 12 months.

In Village Attorney Barry Bright’s absence, Mayor Delonshaw reminded the board that they still needed to approve the FY2027 Tax Levy Ordinance which he had prepared.  The ordinance calls for a 4.9% increase, which affects real estate tax bills assessed in Summer/Fall 2027.  Trustees approved the measure without discussion or dissent.

Also at the October meeting, the board discussed the existing policy that would require new utility customers to pay any remaining unpaid amounts left by previous customers.  It was tentatively agreed that the policy needed to be amended to limit that practice.  Attorney Bright authored a proposed ordinance for trustees consideration.  The new ordinance modifies the utility signup procedures allowing new applicants’ ability to receive utilities services on a property which has prior past due utilities balances still due.  A motion was made and was approved unanimously.

Village Clerk Shannon Hall reviewed the village accounts cash balances and transfers report and explained how she made an adjustment concerning MFT funds.  She also presented information to consider the health insurance renewal for village employees with Blue Cross/Blue Shield and the board approved it without opposition.

As the meeting quickly drew to a close, a question was asked about the nuisance property on Main St.  The house is unoccupied and has open window casings allowing weather and animals free access to the interior.  It was reported that a certified letter was sent to the owner in Indiana, but it remains undelivered as there was no one to accept delivery.

With all business concluded, the meeting adjourned at 6:25pm.

title: ASSESSMENT CHANGES
full_story:
Clay County Supervisor of Assessments, Kindal Eastin, would like to announce that the 2026 Assessment changes have been published.  Property owners that have assessment changes will receive a Notice of Change of Assessment in the mail.

Taxpayers that have any questions or concerns regarding their assessment, please contact the Assessment Office during this time.  All discrepancies of value must be addressed during the 30 days the Board of Review is in session.  Once tax bills are mailed, it is too late to correct any issues based on opinion of value.

If you disagree with your assessment, even if you did not receive a notice, you may file an appeal with the Board of Review within 30 days of publication.  To inquire about how to file, please contact the assessment office at 618-665-3525 extension 5 for a list of the Board of Review Rules and Procedures.  All required forms must be submitted or postmarked by December 11th, or your complaint will not be heard.  The Board of Review cannot hear complaints regarding taxes, only assessed value.

Property owners that wish to review the full publication list, may do so by purchasing a copy of the November 11th, edition of the Clay County Republican.

title: XENIA VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
During public comments, Dawn Gray shared her intentions to open “A Taste of Italy,” a stationary food truck and trailer to be located at 300 Front Street.  Gray told trustees the business is community-driven, women-owned, and centered around heritage, featuring a menu highlighted by wood-fired pizza.  The location will offer outdoor dining with picnic tables and a walk-up or pickup experience, with future plans to expand delivery via DoorDash to Flora and Salem.  Gray estimates the business will launch in the spring of 2027, initially operating on weekends for its first four weeks.

In legislative business, trustees officially passed an ordinance making camping and setting fires on village property unlawful.  The new law follows a discussion from October that stemmed from an interaction between Xenia Police and a homeless individual who had set up camp in the village park.  Meanwhile, an ordinance restricting solicitation within village limits was tabled so trustees could further review the language.

In public safety news, Xenia Police Chief Jerry Burkett reported that the department cruiser participated in the recent “Touch A Truck” event. Burkett also noted there have been no new reports of late-night solicitors over the past week, stating the decrease is likely due to the colder weather.

Turning to village projects, trustees viewed blueprints for a new community building and discussed the next steps toward construction.  Overgrowth treatment at the village ponds was also highlighted, while property updates were tabled with no changes reported.

Additionally, trustees discussed drafting a new ordinance that would allow board members to attend meetings remotely, following a previous discussion regarding trustee commitment and attendance.

Finally, Village Secretary Melissa Eckhart announced that the village has raised 925 dollars so far for the upcoming Ham and Turkey Bingo, with a goal of 1,300 dollars.  The event is scheduled for December 3rd at 6:00 pm at the village hall.

title: SATURDAYS WAGER
full_story:
The Flora Volunteer Fire Department reported on their Facebook page yesterday that a friendly rivalry between West Frankfort and Flora firefighters will benefit a charitable cause following Saturday’s football game.

The Flora Volunteer Fire Department and the West Frankfort Firefighters IAFF Local 2402 have agreed to make matching donations to a cause chosen by the winning side, according to announcements from both fire departments.

If Flora wins, the money will go to the Tyler Schroeder and Tony Doty Scholarship Fund.  The fund supports local students and continues the legacy of two men who meant a great deal to the community and the department.

If West Frankfort wins, the donations will support their work with Project Fire Buddies.  The organization connects firefighters with children facing difficult challenges, with the goal of providing them with “More Good Days”.

The agreement developed over several days of conversations between firefighters, with each side backing its hometown team.

“As you’d expect, they think their team is going to win.  We think our team is going to win,” the Flora Volunteer Fire Department wrote.  “And, well… firefighters being firefighters, one thing led to another.”

Both departments encouraged residents to attend Saturday’s game and support their teams

title: NOMINATION FORMS
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce has opened the nomination period for Business of the year, New Business of the Year, Citizen of the year and Non-Profit organization of the year.

The Chamber Banquet will take place on January 30th and will honor the winning entries.  The Chamber wants people to take time to read the criteria for nomination for all three entries. You also don’t have to nominate someone for each category, but the Chamber would like to have a short essay on why you are nominating that person, new business or business of the year.

Nomination forms can be picked up at the Chamber office or downloaded from the Chambers website.

The deadline to submit nomination forms is this Monday, December 7th. Forms can be emailed to [email protected], mailed to the Chamber office at 223 West Railroad Street or drop it off at the chamber office.

title: ROADSIDE SAFETY CHECK RESULTS
full_story:
Troop 9 Commander Captain Bruce Waggoner announced that troopers issued 14 total citations and arrests, alongside two written warnings during the Roadside Safety Checks in Effingham and Fayette Counties.

The crackdowns focused heavily on taking impaired drivers off the road, resulting in five driving under the influence citations and seven other alcohol or drug-related violations.  Troopers also cited two drivers for license offenses and one for an occupant restraint violation.

State police emphasize that these roadside checks are vital for public safety, noting that alcohol and drug impairment are factors in more than 47% of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  Nationally, an alcohol-related traffic fatality occurs every 39 minutes.

The safety check project was funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.
